# Blog post: multi-window dashboards with Dock Layouts, benefits first

## Context

The operator's goal for the v13.2 release day (2026-10-11): a stunning new blog post that includes the release film, explains the benefits of Dock Layouts for multi-window dashboards, shows a couple of screenshots, and gives code examples of how to use them, in two stages: benefits first, implementation details later. This ticket is stage 1. Stage 2 is its sibling, filed with this one and `blocked_by` it (a genuine two-part series, the one case #13383 reserves `blocked_by` for).

Two 13.2 posts are already on `dev`, both Grace's: `learn/blog/a-workspace-that-can-leave-its-window.md` (#9854 → #19507; thesis: move the application, not the messages, so every window is a render target; one minimal Dock Layout example; stills from the film take) and `learn/blog/one-repository-per-reader.md` (#19495 → #19508, the split). Neither carries the film, which was not published yet, and neither is written from the dashboard builder's side: what do my users get when panes can leave the window, and what do I write to give it to them?

## The Problem

Dock Layouts are the centerpiece of 13.2 (release notes TL;DR, #14800). A cold reader who builds dashboards (operations consoles, monitoring walls, analytics screens: the shape the Workstation demo takes) needs three things, in this order:

1. **What their users get:** a workspace each user arranges (tabs, splits, edge rails); panes that leave as real OS windows onto a second monitor and come home; the same live pane on every screen (no reload, no re-fetch, no sync protocol); one Undo across windows; Reset; saved arrangements.
2. **What it costs the developer:** panes are ordinary component configs, zones place them, persistence stores documents, never DOM.
3. **Where it stops:** honest bounds (the browser's popup permission, SharedWorkers are same-origin, what the film does not show).

The film shows (1). The post makes (2) concrete with code a reader can run, and links the guides for depth.

## The Architectural Reality

Sources, all public, all on `dev`:
- Guides `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts*.md` (DockLayouts, Adoption, Features, Mechanics, Panes, StateAndPersistence, Styling, Windows) and the tutorial `learn/tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout.md` (live, editable examples).
- The engine: `src/dashboard/dock/` (`Workspace.mjs` and its packages); ADR 0029 (docking design).
- The demo: `apps/workstation`; the screenshots come from it at the release head.
- The release notes `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.2.0.md` (#14800) and the film #15252, which Emmy publishes to YouTube with its cover image (the same embed the README and the notes get).
- Portal: `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json` (manual registration); post images live in `neomjs/pages` under `resources_pub/website/blog/`.

## The Fix

- `learn/blog/<slug>.md`: a thesis-first hero piece per the `blog-post` skill. The film is the opening proof; 2–4 new screenshots of dashboard arrangements (one spanning two OS windows); 2–3 code examples (declare a workspace; a dashboard pane catalog with rails and window tear-out; save and restore an arrangement), each verified against the release head; links into the guides and Grace's architecture post instead of repeating them.
- Register the post in `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json`.
- New images land in `neomjs/pages` first (a pages PR); the post links their raw URLs, as the 13.2 notes do.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The post is on `dev`, registered in `blog.json` (parses), and renders at `#/news/blog/blog/<slug>`; every Mermaid diagram is render-verified.
- [ ] The film is embedded from YouTube with its cover image, matching the README/notes embed.
- [ ] ≥ 2 new screenshots of dashboard arrangements, ≥ 1 spanning two OS windows, each with alt text and a caption.
- [ ] ≥ 2 code examples, each verified to run against the release head (the PR states how).
- [ ] Every external claim is sourced; the five over-claim flavors are audited; the title passes the skill's mechanical title test.
- [ ] ≥ 2 model reviews, ≥ 1 from a non-Claude family; the operator approves last.
- [ ] Zero client names.

## Out of Scope

- Stage 2 (implementation details): the sibling ticket.
- Editing Grace's posts (her surface): cross-links only.
- Distribution (private; out of scope for #13383 too).
- Publishing the film (Emmy's lane).
